hist-afr-02-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2019). Great Zimbabwe. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-afr-02-c2.quote: Blinded by their racism, they could not bring themselves to believe that such a place could have been built by black Africans.
hist-afr-02-c2.claim: European colonialists initially refused to believe it had been built by Africans, attributing it to Phoenicians or other outsiders.

hist-afr-04-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2026). Berlin Conference 1884-5: Establishing the Rules of the Scramble for Africa. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-afr-04-c1.quote: by 1914, the whole continent of Africa, with the exception of Abyssinia and Liberia, came under European control.
hist-afr-04-c1.claim: By 1914, only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent.

hist-afr-03-c2.text: Nathan Nunn, Leonard Wantchekon (2009). The Slave Trade and the Origins of Mistrust in Africa. NBER Working Paper 14783.
hist-afr-03-c2.quote: Combining contemporary household survey data with historic data on slave shipments, we show that individuals whose ancestors were heavily raided during the slave trade today exhibit less trust in neighbors, relatives, and their local government.
hist-afr-03-c2.claim: Recent economic-history research (Nathan Nunn) finds long-term negative effects on trust and economic development in regions most affected by the trade.

hist-afr-03-c2.text: Joshua J. Mark (2025). Transatlantic Slave Trade: The Shame of Nations. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-afr-03-c2.quote: Just because the transatlantic slave trade had been abolished in Great Britain in 1807 and the United States in 1808, did not mean slavers stopped engaging in it.
hist-afr-03-c2.claim: The Atlantic slave trade was banned by Britain in 1807 and the US in 1808 (though smuggling continued); abolition of slavery itself came later (UK 1833, US 1865, Brazil 1888).

hist-afr-05-c2.quote: The start of trading under the AfCFTA Agreement began on January 1 2021.
hist-afr-05-c2.claim: Africa's Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA, 2021) aims to integrate African economies, currently more interlinked with former colonial powers than each other.

hist-afr-05-c3.quote: Based on the results of the five IRC studies, we now estimate that 5.4 million excess deaths have occurred between August 1998 and April 2007.
hist-afr-05-c3.claim: Major conflicts include the Congo wars (Africa's deadliest since WWII, an estimated ~5 million dead, a widely cited but contested figure), Darfur, Boko Haram, Tigray.
